title: Direct versus indirect hot-water cylinders | G3 Hot-Water Knowledge
description: Understand direct versus indirect hot-water cylinders with clear model-aware information and practical questions for your cylinder engineer.
answer: A direct cylinder heats stored water electrically; an indirect cylinder mainly uses a heat-exchanger coil supplied by another heat source. Configuration matters.

sections.heading: The key distinction
paragraphs: The difference changes fault diagnosis and replacement planning. An indirect appliance may depend on a connected boiler, valve and hot-water demand. A direct appliance may depend on timed electrical supplies and immersion controls. Backup elements do not make every system identical.

sections.heading: Apply the information to the installed system
paragraphs: Before changing the cylinder type, assess the heat source, supply, electrical arrangement, household demand and installation. Solar or heat-pump designs may have further model-specific requirements and should not be chosen by the words direct or indirect alone.

sections.heading: A practical next question
paragraphs: Gather the full model, heating method, recent symptoms and available paperwork. Discuss the scope with a person competent for the actual work. Technical information here supports that conversation and is not a substitute for manufacturer instructions or individual system assessment.

faqs.question: Can the same no-hot-water enquiry follow different diagnostic paths on direct and indirect cylinders?
faqs.answer: Yes. Electrical heating paths matter on a direct cylinder, while the connected heat source and coil controls matter on an indirect system.
